clue.text: Space bears with hair? Some kind of mystery

indicators.note: in a down clue, a thing that bears another carries it on top, so the second part is placed above the first

blocks.note: having locks, as a fancy word for possessing hair
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a hairy bear in some space, before admitting it is all a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are tresses, so 'with hair' is LOCKED; because this is a down clue, ROOM bears LOCKED, with LOCKED sitting above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A locked room mystery is a classic detective sub-genre where a crime happens in a sealed chamber.

clue.text: Hot, always, fish sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its slices, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A seafood snack that is always served hot, fish in sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running a fever feels hot, so feverish describes a raised temperature.

clue.text: Recommend inhaling e-cigarette

indicators.note: breathing something in takes it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: to refer someone to a person is to recommend them
the letter that prefixes the vaping device's name

explanation.surface: Advice to take up vaping with an electronic cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'e-cigarette': the E is the inhaled letter and 'cigarette' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis joint, a kind of illicit smoke.

clue.text: Trend in retirement is correct

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

blocks.note: the tide of opinion is its trend

explanation.surface: A claim that a fashion for retiring early is the right one.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct its errors before publication, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Adoring a suitor with old pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are judged poor and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fond admirer turns up wearing antique underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is British slang for rubbish, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatrous means worshipping excessively, a strong form of blind reverence and devotion.

clue.text: Console with cool look after cutting negative comment

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes between its parts, so the first words sit inside

blocks.note: to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: Trying to soothe someone with a cool look after a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' reads as describing the remark, but it tells the first two words to split the refusal in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo makes games consoles such as the Switch, so the brand name stands for a console.

clue.text: Calls up about opening in pelvis getting infected

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to cite is to call up as evidence or summon

explanation.surface: A doctor's report on someone phoned about a pelvic wound turning infected.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into CITES to give CITPES, which then reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic describes a wound contaminated by bacteria, so it means infected.

clue.text: Boss elephant's first to leave

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name
the letter that leaves is taken out of the word

blocks.note: first letter of the elephant's name

explanation.surface: A boss elephant, the herd leader, is the first to go.
explanation.walkthrough: DUMBO loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the raised central knob on a shield, also called its boss.

clue.text: Golf tournament finished without a clear resolution

blocks.note: the Open is golf's major championship

explanation.surface: A golf tournament finished with no clear winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is the British Open golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-ended means having no fixed limit or conclusion, so it lacks a settled outcome.

clue.text: Apple's torch possibly gets strong support

blocks.note: Apple names its products with a lower-case i, as in iPhone
a torch gives out a beam of light

explanation.surface: Praise for the flashlight on an Apple phone being powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-beam is a steel girder with an I-shaped cross section used in building frames.

clue.text: Work out Carry On film's 25% sex?

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, here the opening one

blocks.note: to keep on is to carry on
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A query about how much sex is in a Carry On film, the bawdy British comedy series.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films are cheeky British comedies; here the words simply mean continue.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep fit is exercise to maintain fitness, so it is a noun for a workout.

clue.text: Frozen song title - animated success

indicators.note: something animated is set moving, so these letters are stirred about

blocks.note: to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: A note that the title song of Frozen was a hit for the animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' seems to describe the Disney film, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Go is the best-known number from Disney's film Frozen, sung by Elsa.

clue.text: Flatter doctor leading Iowa's premier emergency room

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: ER is the American abbreviation for an emergency room

explanation.surface: A medic is praised for leading the top emergency unit in Iowa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a verb meaning praise; it is the comparative of flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and dry both describe a dull, unemotional manner, so the comparatives match.

clue.text: Cabin littered with a lot of plants

indicators.note: things littered are strewn about untidily, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden shed cluttered with a large number of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of plants' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'of plants'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical is the adjective for the study and world of vegetation and flora.

clue.text: Poison label absurd on kebab we're told

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense, so the letters are jumbled
what we are told is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: a doner is a kebab of spit-roasted meat

explanation.surface: A ridiculous warning sticker on a takeaway kebab says it is poison.
explanation.walkthrough: A doner kebab is the late-night takeaway; said in a non-rhotic accent it matches the Italian word for lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna, or deadly nightshade, is a highly toxic plant and the drug made from it.

clue.text: Aeroflot use a terminal inspiring pleasure seeker

indicators.note: inspiring here means breathing in, so the words take the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A hedonist chooses to fly the Russian airline from a particular terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, lotus-eaters live in idle bliss, so the term describes someone devoted to luxury and indolence.

clue.text: Mo Salah regularly hit goalpost after ditching second suspect eye doctor

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
ditching means throwing away, so that letter is removed
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The Liverpool footballer keeps striking the woodwork, so maybe he needs his eyes checked.
explanation.walkthrough: One S, the abbreviation for second, is removed from the collected letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophthalmologist is a medical specialist in diseases and surgery of the eyes.

clue.text: Country house had a nice bust inside

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are smashed into a new order
inside places the jumbled word within the others

explanation.surface: A stately home had an attractive sculpted head on display indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a statue in the house, but means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate with a main residence in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Send down naughty child, overturning respectful denial

indicators.note: turning over flips the phrase so its letters read the other way

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a polite refusal addressed to a man

explanation.surface: A misbehaving child is sent to their room after rudely contradicting a polite refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' is British for jailing someone, as well as expelling a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To send down is British slang for a court sentencing someone to jail.

clue.text: American substitutes for magicians' silver band?

indicators.note: one thing substituting for another takes its place in the word

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An American stand-in for a magic act's silver ring, as in a conjuring trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'silver band' looks like a magic ring; the question mark flags that band is a group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of players performing music together, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Cut back Southern press

blocks.note: to crimp is to press into folds or ridges

explanation.surface: A newspaper in the South makes budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut back' might suggest reversal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise hard, reducing spending to save money.

clue.text: "Greasy peppermill on the counter" claims 17th century journalist?

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the words hold the answer within them
counter means going against the usual direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A news report quoting a complaint about an oily pepper grinder on the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the diarist kept a journal rather than writing for papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary in the 1660s, a journal in the literal sense.

clue.text: Object in SpaceX with peak returns

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters read the other way

blocks.note: only the final X counts here, the Roman numeral for ten
an alp is a mountain peak

explanation.surface: A SpaceX launch returns with its payload at a high point.
explanation.walkthrough: The company name SpaceX is split: 'Space' ends the definition and X gives the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a large body orbiting a star, a celestial thing out among the stars.

clue.text: Mount exercise to prepare missile

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill
to do food is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A military order to stage a drill getting a weapon ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon fired at ships.

clue.text: Picked up bit of a fork in the river

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves part of a broken fork from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is the river through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is a major river of north-east England flowing through Newcastle.

clue.text: Glastonbury headliner is, in short, owed a large beer

indicators.note: making a word short cuts off its final letter

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A festival star is, briefly, owed a big pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is England's biggest music festival; DUE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dua Lipa, the pop singer, topped the bill on the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival in 2024.

clue.text: Start to pile mixture of earth and water over ditch

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
turned over, the letters of this down entry read upwards

explanation.surface: Instructions to heap sludge over a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like the place being filled, but it is the verb for getting rid of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to discard it, the same as ditching it.

clue.text: Say Bedouin's name in French, Bill?

blocks.note: an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A question asking what the desert people are called in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' shows Bedouin is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are desert Arabs traditionally living as wanderers with their herds.

clue.text: Less sensitive individual could be a leader

explanation.surface: A less thin-skinned person might make a good boss.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is pronounced to rhyme with 'plumber', meaning more numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the top person in charge, the boss or chief.
